races.name: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Race

runners_data.name: South Dakota
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for A P O'Brien and Wayne Lordan, consistently placed (4-4-3-3) on Good ground though yet to win, this 7½f trip is the longest attempted and the strong pace engineered by the four front-runners sets things up ideally for a late run.

runners_data.name: Full Volume
runners_data.note: Race-winner over 8f on Good going for Mrs Harrington, trained to target this trip with a natural front-running style; the key question is whether she can survive a four-way pace battle in the first half of the race before asserting her class in the straight.

runners_data.name: Joga Bonito
runners_data.note: Won impressively over 7f on Soft for Twomey and wore a hood (p) here, suggesting some keenness to manage; her best form has come on softer ground and the switch to Good is worth monitoring, though her near-side draw and front-running style mean she will be involved early regardless.

runners_data.name: Lars Soldier
runners_data.note: Busy campaign (six runs, 13-day turnaround) for a small yard with decent 14-day form (2/12), but his prominent style and proven ability on Good going make him a key beneficiary if the pace-setters implode; never won beyond 5f is the slight distance concern at 7½f.

runners_data.name: Ruler's Control
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner among the pace group at OR=100 and wears a tongue-tie; sole career win came on Heavy ground and he has struggled on Good (0W0P in 2 sim-going runs), which is a meaningful caveat despite his class advantage on official ratings.

runners_data.name: Cudawudashuda
runners_data.note: Lightly raced (one run) at OR=120 for the powerful G M Lyons-Colin Keane combination; ran sixth over 8f on Good last time but that bare form is almost meaningless given the unexposed profile — the booking of Keane alone signals connections expect a forward showing.

runners_data.name: Panhandle
runners_data.note: OR=120 but backed by a dismal recent form string (00, finishing 13th and 14th on Good ground) and is tagged as a front-runner who fades; given the likely early pace battle, this horse could burn out badly and becomes a genuine pace-collapse enabler rather than a winner candidate.

runners_data.name: The Long Haul
runners_data.note: Placed fifth on debut over 8f on Good but then finished 12th over 6f; the step back up to 7½f is logical and McCourt's 14-day strike rate (1/12) is modest — looks exposed relative to the more unexposed OR=120 runners and needs significant improvement.

runners_data.name: Wunderschon
runners_data.note: Single run (7th over 7f on Good) for the Harrington yard alongside stablemate Full Volume; unknown style (U), lightly raced, and ridden by a 5lb claimer Keithen Kennedy — connections' second string here, but the OR=120 mark leaves room for surprise if the race develops unusually.

races.paceDynamic: Panhandle, Full Volume, and Joga Bonito are all confirmed front-runners in a nine-runner field, and Ruler's Control adds a fourth pace presence, making a strong, unrelenting gallop over 7½ furlongs on Good ground at Roscommon a near-certainty. The pace duel is likely to ignite from the break as these four contest for the early lead, ensuring the field is strung out and stamina reserves are burned through the middle section of the race. Ruler's Control, the highest-rated of the pace group on OR=100, and Full Volume, a proven race-winner at the distance, are best positioned among the leaders to survive if the pace becomes self-destructive, but a sustained gallop of this nature sets the race up classically for horses tracking from midfield or making late runs. Hold-up and prominent-but-patient horses — most notably South Dakota (H) and Lars Soldier (P) — are most favoured by this pace shape, as they can exploit tiring leaders in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the four-way pace battle burns out the leaders, freeing held-up horses to power through.
scenarios.body: South Dakota, running from the hold-up position for A P O'Brien and Wayne Lordan, is ideally poised to swoop late as the pace implodes in the straight, having shown consistent form on Good going. Lars Soldier, prominent but patient for Wesley Joyce, can also pick off weakening leaders as the race distance tests the early pace-setters.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Survives Strong Pace
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners proves classiest and controls tempo without fully burning out.
scenarios.body: Full Volume (OR=96, race-winner over 8f on Good, strong jockey in Shane Foley) is best equipped among the pace setters to dictate from the front and still have enough petrol to hold on late. Joga Bonito has won on soft and placed on good ground; if she settles slightly off the battle and pings clear, the step up to 7½f suits her profile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Quickens Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong but not suicidal, allowing a prominent-tracking horse to pounce before the closers organise.
scenarios.body: Lars Soldier has the tactical flexibility to sit just off the frantic lead group and challenge from a forward position once those in front crack, his quick turnaround (13 days) suggesting trainer confidence. Cudawudashuda (OR=120, Colin Keane) is lightly raced and completely unexposed — if Lyons has a well-kept juvenile here, a prominent-to-winner run from the highest-rated runner in the field cannot be ruled out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Moderate, Leaders Hold
scenarios.trigger: If Panhandle and Ruler's Control fade early and Full Volume or Joga Bonito face less pressure than anticipated, allowing a front-runner to steal.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires at least two of the four pace horses to disengage, effectively gifting a lone leader an uncontested run — unlikely given the competitive nature of each runner's connections. Ruler's Control, a winner on Heavy who is stepping up markedly in class, remains the wildcard if he dictates in a scenario of unexpected calm.

watchPoints.text: Panhandle has finished 13th and 14th on both recent Good-ground starts and is tagged as a pace horse who fades — watch whether he fires out early and then collapses, as this is the primary trigger for the closers to pounce late.

Cudawudashuda carries OR=120 and Colin Keane for G M Lyons off a 59-day break with just one run to his name — a lightly raced, well-bred juvenile with a top booking is the classic dark-horse profile in a race like this.

Full Volume must contend with at least three rivals (Panhandle, Joga Bonito, Ruler's Control) for the early lead — watch the first two furlongs to see who blinks first and whether she can reach a position of control before the real race begins.

Ruler's Control wears a tongue-tie and has zero wins or places from two starts on Good going; if he contests the early pace and fades, the projected Pace Dynamic collapses into a two-horse lead battle, significantly altering how the race unfolds for mid-field runners.

South Dakota for A P O'Brien has been placed in all four career starts without winning — Wayne Lordan will need to time the challenge perfectly off what should be a genuine gallop to finally get the juvenile off the mark at the seventh time of asking.

races.name: Elphin Handicap

runners_data.name: Givehertilxmas
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer trained by Gerard Keane returning after 62 days; has shown ability on Good going (sim 4/11) but never won, and will need a clear passage from the rear in a very congested field at Roscommon.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Pairc
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type with consistent Good-ground form but a consistent record of placing without winning (9/12 sim-going); recent 11d turnaround for W J Lee is positive, but finishing position will depend entirely on traffic from the back.

runners_data.name: Angel Of Promise
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with a ⚠ fade flag who drops back from a 50-day break; the tendency to weaken in the finish is a significant concern in a race where closers need to sustain their run over 7½f on Good.

runners_data.name: Shamanka
runners_data.note: Hold-up style horse who showed a useful 4th recently at 5f; stepping up to 7½f may test stamina, and with a 5lb claimer aboard the handicap weight looks manageable, but the trip extension is untested in recent form.

runners_data.name: Brains
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in the race and likely to control the early pace unopposed; however, the STYLE_FIT tag (0.94) notes a horse racing out of its most effective role, and at 10 years old with a pattern of mid-placed finishes rather than winning, the value here is in how it shapes the race rather than winning it.

runners_data.name: Cisterna
runners_data.note: Competitively-rated 3yo with a win on Good over 8f (1W2P sim-going); the owner-trainer Slattery combination adds intrigue and the horse has placed multiple times in similar conditions, making it one of the more interesting mid-division types if it gets a clean run.

runners_data.name: James Henry
runners_data.note: A genuine deep hold-up horse by nature who has been redistributed to midfield on the map due to field congestion; the STYLE_FIT (0.91) tempers expectation, and a 7-year-old with recent form of 3-3000 suggests consistency at a level rather than an upward move.

runners_data.name: Glen Breeze
runners_data.note: Has a win and three places on Good going in recent form (1W3P sim-going) and is a natural hold-up type pushed into a midfield mapping here; if able to find a prominent-enough position in running, this 3yo for Patrick Magee has legitimate claims.

runners_data.name: Whatswrongnow
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a strong placing record (0W5P) on Good and regularly runs competitive races at 5-6f; the step up to 7½f is a question given all recent starts have been at shorter, but the style suits a Brains-led scenario perfectly.

runners_data.name: Oitentinha
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a ⚠ fade flag returning after 73 days for Oliver McKiernan; the redistribution to midfield reflects the crowded hold-up section, and fading form combined with a lengthy break makes this a very speculative participant.

runners_data.name: Queen Of Newark
runners_data.note: A 3yo hold-up type with a ⚠ fade flag who has not won and struggled at trip and going in recent starts; redistributed to midfield on the map, the form profile (0-0300) gives little confidence she can run a race-winning finishing kick at 7½f.

runners_data.name: Tamazu
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up horse returning from a 361-day layoff for Fergal Birrane, which immediately elevates risk; best form was on Soft/Standard going (sim-going 5/15) and the Good conditions here are far from ideal alongside the fitness concern.

runners_data.name: Sunday Sovereign
runners_data.note: Prominent-style 9-year-old with a ⚠ fade flag after 87 days off; showed a 3rd over 8f on Soft but has a poor record on Good (12/15 sim-going), and the combination of going concerns, long absence and fade tendency makes this hard to support.

runners_data.name: La Campanella
runners_data.note: Hold-up type by nature, redistributed to midfield; headgear (visor) noted, and six days since last run for Gerard Keane could indicate freshness, but recent form (075474) and a weak sim-going score (4/11) suggest she needs things to fall right.

runners_data.name: Bullet Bourbon
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up horse who won over 7f on Standard but has struggled on Good (sim 8/15); the redistribution to midfield is the practical reality here, and while the win pedigree is there, Good turf may not bring out the best.

runners_data.name: Gordon Bennett
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse for Peter Fahey with a 3rd on his best recent run; sits in midfield on the map due to redistribution (STYLE_FIT 0.90), and without a jockey listed in the data the angle is unclear, though the Fahey yard has placed form on offer.

runners_data.name: Draiocht
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a recent 3rd and 4th on Good going for T J O'Mara; redistributed to midfield, this 6-year-old has been running with some regularity (6d since last run) and shows enough consistency to feature without necessarily winning.

runners_data.name: Distillate
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse with a 2nd from 7 starts on Standard for Adrian McGuinness (T14:3/21 shows strong yard activity); the most recent run was a B (fell/brought down), which clouds fitness, and sim-going form on Good is weak (5/15), making this hard to strongly advocate despite the trainer's current form.

races.paceDynamic: Brains is the one confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner field and, crucially, is unlikely to face serious early pressure from genuine rivals for the lead, meaning the pace is expected to be controlled and sustainable rather than pressured or breakneck. Whatswrongnow and Sunday Sovereign are the only other prominent-profile types, but neither is a habitual pace-setter, so Brains should dictate a measured gallop through Roscommon's 7½f on Good ground. The bulk of this field — Givehertilxmas, Cisterna, Phoenix Pairc, Glen Breeze, Distillate, Gordon Bennett and many others — are true hold-up or midfield horses by nature, and with so many of them competing for the same real estate in the latter half of the field, the race will become a bunched, traffic-dependent cavalry charge in the final two furlongs. This race shape — a controlled early pace with a wall of closers converging — favours horses that can travel prominently just off the single leader or secure a clean mid-division passage with a clear run, rather than deep closers buried in traffic who need a truly strong gallop to be delivered late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Brains Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Brains sets a comfortable, uncontested lead and the prominent duo behind can find a clean position and rattle home.
scenarios.body: Brains dictates the fractions on Good ground over 7½f, and the horse or horses sitting second or third have an unobstructed passage to the line, getting first run on the hold-up horde. Whatswrongnow and Sunday Sovereign are the obvious prominent-type beneficiaries if they can slot in behind the leader, as the moderate pace suits those who can travel and pounce without needing a true test.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to string the field and a horse tracking mid-division finds a gap in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With 18 runners funnelling into Roscommon's straight, a horse settled in a handy mid-division berth with a clear passage will get first run on the deep closers while the leader is caught. Cisterna has won over this type of trip on Good and showed a good recent fifth, while Glen Breeze and Gordon Bennett are class hold-up types that may manage to secure a better-than-mapped position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Deep Closer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unexpectedly strong and the hold-up horses get a fast enough gallop to be delivered with a single run.
scenarios.body: Should Brains go off quicker than anticipated, or if prominent types push the tempo, the deep closers could get the genuine pace scenario they need to finish through beaten horses. Givehertilxmas, Phoenix Pairc and Distillate are genuine hold-up types by nature, but this scenario is marked down because many of the supposed closers are redistributed horses whose natural position is further forward, reducing the likelihood of a true late sweep.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Brains is allowed to dictate a very modest gallop and the hold-up horses cannot close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: In a race with only one genuine pace-setter and a sustainable tempo, Brains could simply control throughout and prove too hard to peg back for the closing horde. This is the least likely scenario given the horse is racing out of role at a STYLE_FIT of 0.94 and the sheer volume of closers in behind, but at 10 years old on a flat track with no rival to pressure it, a soft lead cannot be entirely dismissed.

watchPoints.text: Whatswrongnow is the key prominent-type to watch — if Sam Coen on Brains allows a very steady pace, Whatswrongnow could steal a crucial position just off the leader and get first run on the entire hold-up field in a race with no other natural pace horses.

Traffic in the final two furlongs is the single biggest race-shaping factor — with at least 10 genuine hold-up horses converging from behind in an 18-runner Roscommon field, watch for any horse drawn wide enough to avoid the inside pile-up, as a clean outside passage could be decisive.

Cisterna warrants close attention: the owner-trainer combination, a win on Good going over 8f, and multiple recent placings suggest this 3yo is competing near the top of its form, and any midfield position with daylight could see it produce a strong finish.

Glen Breeze has won and placed on Good going three times recently — despite being mapped to midfield due to redistribution, if Patrick Magee's runner can secure a closer-to-prominent position than the map suggests, the recent form profile makes it a live contender.

Tamazu's 361-day layoff is the most extreme fitness flag in the race and is worth monitoring in the early market moves — if support comes despite the absence, it may signal a yard that has had this horse purposefully prepared; if it drifts, treat accordingly.

races.name: Lidan Handicap

runners_data.name: Eddie G
runners_data.note: Recent back-to-back wins over 7f on Good ground are highly relevant; Sam Coen (5) takes off valuable weight, and Adrian McGuinness's yard is in decent form (T14: 3/21); prominent style suits perfectly here and 34 days since last run is no concern.

runners_data.name: Engines On
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago (LR: 2d) which is an obvious freshness question on any horse, and his recent form shows a string of midfield finishes before a sole win on Soft ground; prominent style is right but the quick turnaround and trainer's cold run (T14: 0/4) are negatives.

runners_data.name: Plume Noire
runners_data.note: Returning from a massive 352-day absence, so fitness must be the primary question regardless of any other positives; hold-up style on a track where the race shape favours prominent racers compounds the concern, though Good ground is clearly suitable based on all recent form.

runners_data.name: Earls
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at 8f on Good and Soft ground for Gavin Cromwell with Gary Carroll aboard; prominent style is well suited to the expected race shape, though the step down to 7½f from recent 8f starts and zero wins from the last six runs is a mild negative.

runners_data.name: Tokyo Treasure
runners_data.note: All six career runs have come on Good ground (sim-going: 6/6), making the surface a genuine positive; prominent style fits the shape but the last run produced a 13th and recent form is mixed — the 4-year-old needs to find improvement.

runners_data.name: Goal Exceeded
runners_data.note: Two wins from the last six starts at 7f on Good ground make this hold-up performer the most credible closer in the field; Adrian McGuinness double-handed on the card (see Eddie G), and 22 days since last run is straightforward — the key is whether the pace is strong enough to suit.

runners_data.name: Gavoo
runners_data.note: Consistent place-getter on Good ground over shorter trips; stepping up to 7½f is a query for a horse whose best form is over 6f, and the hold-up style may leave too much to do against a controlled Punica Granatum pace — headgear (b) noted.

runners_data.name: Morehampton
runners_data.note: J P Murtagh's 3-year-old has a hold-up profile but a mixed recent record, most runs coming over 6-7f on Good ground; the 24-day break is fine, but a step up to 7½f while racing from the rear in a field where the leader may not be caught is a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Punica Granatum
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner; Shane Foley is the key booking and the Harrington yard has two winners from 28 in 14 days (T14: 2/28); hold-up pedigree on paper but all evidence confirms a front-running role — the sole question is whether 7½f on Good ground stretches stamina after previous form at shorter.

runners_data.name: Highbury See See
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose natural rearward position cannot be replicated in this field — pushed into a midfield mapping because the race holds too many closers; Slattery-trained and self-ridden, with 66 days off, and the style fit discount (0.92) reflects real race-shape risk.

runners_data.name: Merisi Diamond
runners_data.note: Returned to winning form last time over 7f on Soft ground but that was 134 days ago, and all recent best form comes on Soft or Heavy rather than Good — the sim-going record (3/15 on comparable ground) is a clear flag; prominent style suits the shape but going may not.

runners_data.name: Mercurial
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer that the density of front-running types has pushed out of its preferred position in the mapping (style fit: 0.93); Seamie Heffernan is a strong booking and the horse has placed at 6f on Good, but racing a length further back than ideal in a 13-runner field limits the chance considerably.

runners_data.name: Ninth Crusade
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride on this O'Callaghan 3-year-old who naturally wants to race handy but is displaced rearward by the size and shape of this field (style fit: 0.91); Good-ground form over 7f showed a recent third, making him interesting on form alone, but the tactical disadvantage is real and must temper expectations.

races.paceDynamic: Punica Granatum is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Shane Foley in the plate, is virtually certain to stride into the lead from the outset on this flat Roscommon 7½f track, setting a measured, controlled tempo that is unlikely to be challenged from the front. Behind him, Eddie G, Engines On, Earls, and Tokyo Treasure all want to race prominently, meaning the early order from second place backwards will be competitive and slightly pressured, but the leader himself should enjoy a comfortable, uncontested gallop. This field carries more hold-up and prominent horses than the race shape can accommodate in their natural positions — Mercurial and Ninth Crusade, both genuine prominent/hold-up types, along with Highbury See See, are mapped to midfield because they simply cannot all get to the front in a 13-runner field, and their chances are materially reduced as a result. The race shape therefore strongly favours horses who can travel prominently in the slipstream of an uncontested leader and pick them off in the final two furlongs, making a prominent racer with good tactical position and the stamina to see out the 7½f on Good ground the most advantaged profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Punica Granatum Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Punica Granatum leads without pressure and Foley dictates a comfortable tempo, allowing the leader to conserve energy for a sustained finish.
scenarios.body: Punica Granatum sets an uncontested pace on Good ground, dictating throughout and kicking again at the two-furlong pole before rivals can organise a challenge; horses travelling prominently just behind benefit most as they get a clear run in second gear before the sprint home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough that Punica Granatum ties up late and a prominent chaser swoops in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The cluster of prominent horses racing in the slipstream — particularly those with proven Good-ground form at the trip — are perfectly placed to collar a tiring leader inside the final furlong; Eddie G's recent back-to-back wins at 7f on Good ground and Earls' consistent placing record make them the likeliest beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong enough to string the field out and create a late-closing opportunity for a genuine hold-up type.
scenarios.body: Goal Exceeded has won twice recently at this trip on Good turf and can come from off the pace when a true gallop is set; however, Highbury See See and Ninth Crusade are mapped out of their natural hold-up position and their redistributed placement significantly reduces their ability to deliver a typical late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Exploits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group scrimmage for position in the early stages, causing interference and opening a gap for a forgotten runner.
scenarios.body: A messy, bunched early phase in a 13-runner field on a flat track can occasionally produce a gap for a horse finding its stride late; Merisi Diamond, returning from 134 days off but winning last time on Soft, and Morehampton represent low-probability alternatives if the race falls apart tactically.

watchPoints.text: Engines On ran just two days ago — watch the paddock and early movement carefully, as any signs of flatness or a slow break from a prominent-style horse could compromise his chance and open gaps for those behind.

Mercurial and Ninth Crusade are both genuine prominent horses who will likely be trapped further back than they want — if either gets shuffled wide hunting for a run in the first half-mile, they could unsettle neighbours and disrupt the race shape.

Merisi Diamond's going suitability is borderline — if the track is riding faster than Good and the race develops at a strong clip, the horse's Soft-ground form becomes significantly less relevant and its chance deflates sharply.

Punica Granatum's early stride pattern is the key tell for the entire race — if Foley allows a true solo lead without looking over his shoulder, the race is set up for stalking prominent types; if the leader is bustled along, the scenario shifts toward closers.

Plume Noire returns from 352 days off — watch whether the yard has produced any public trial evidence or gallop reports, as a fresh eight-year-old hold-up horse represents a very live drifter in the market if fitness is not confirmed.

races.name: Lecarrow Race

runners_data.name: Hazdann
runners_data.note: Trained by D K Weld and ridden by Chris Hayes, this four-year-old has won and placed on Good ground in similar prominent-style races, making him the model fit for the anticipated race shape; his 85-day absence is worth monitoring but Weld runners return well-prepared and his course-distance form at 9f on Good is encouraging.

runners_data.name: God Of Power
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and rides this three-year-old, who carries a lightly-used record including a win at 7f on Good; his natural instinct is to race prominently but with Handshake taking an uncontested lead and others also wanting to be handy, he is likely to find himself racing further back than ideal, which the 0.92 style-fit flag reflects.

runners_data.name: Handshake
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's yard is firing with 12 winners from 71 runners in the past 14 days, and Handshake — who won over 8f on Soft at Sligo — is the clear pace-maker here; his style-fit of 0.90 reflects that he is being asked to lead rather than sit prominently, but on this evidence he should do so unchallenged and he steps up in trip with the tongue tie in place.

runners_data.name: Dial Me In
runners_data.note: The only genuine hold-up horse in the race, Dial Me In has form figures that include a runner-up finish on Good ground and handles 10f, but his chance is structurally constrained by the likelihood that Handshake will set only a steady gallop — he needs pace ahead of him to close into, and this race may not provide it; tongue tie applied.

runners_data.name: Sinmara
runners_data.note: This three-year-old owns a win at 8f on Soft and has hit the frame on Good, but she is a prominent-by-nature runner who the pace map cannot accommodate in her preferred slot given how many similar types are entered; racing further back than her form suggests she likes will be a genuine test of adaptability, and the 0.93 style-fit discount reflects that reality.

races.paceDynamic: Handshake is the lone confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine rival for the lead — he should settle comfortably into a relaxed, uncontested gallop on Good ground over 1m2½f at Roscommon. Hazdann is the only other horse genuinely mapped to a prominent position and will track Handshake, while Dial Me In is the sole authentic hold-up type and will be ridden from the rear. The field actually contains more prominent-minded horses than can all achieve their natural position: Sinmara and God Of Power are true front-running or prominent types who are likely to be pushed back into midfield roles they do not naturally suit, making their chances in shapes that require that position harder to realise. With Handshake controlling a moderate, sustainable tempo from the front and no horse likely to press him hard early, this race shape strongly favours horses who can sit close to the pace and sustain their effort — the prominent tracker profile, exemplified by Hazdann, is ideally placed to exploit a controlled gallop that may not test genuine hold-up horses sufficiently.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Handshake Controls, Hazdann Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Handshake sets an uncontested, measured pace and the race is decided by those closest to him in the straight.
scenarios.body: Handshake dictates a comfortable rhythm and the race develops as a test of sustained galloping rather than a finishing sprint, perfectly suiting horses who have been on the pace throughout; Hazdann, with a win at 7f on Good and strong prominent-style form, is ideally positioned to pounce when Handshake is challenged in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Handshake Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Handshake's front-running tactics produce a true test of stamina and none of the chasers can close the gap.
scenarios.body: Handshake, stepping up to 1m2½f on turf after winning at 8f, finds the extra distance suiting his relaxed front-running style and the pace is strong enough to drain his rivals' finishing kicks; the horse with the highest OR in the race and a recent win at a similar grade has the class to simply outstay this field from the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Dial Me In Finishes Fastest
scenarios.trigger: If Handshake sets a genuinely strong pace that stretches the field and creates a fast-closing opportunity for hold-up runners.
scenarios.body: Dial Me In is the only authentic hold-up runner in the race and would be the prime beneficiary if the front-runners burn each other out; his form includes a runner-up finish on Good ground and he handles this trip, but the redistribution of Sinmara and God Of Power away from their natural positions means the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to deliver this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Disrupted Pace, Scrambled Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Sinmara or God Of Power contests the lead early and the race shape fractures unexpectedly.
scenarios.body: Though both Sinmara and God Of Power are redistributed away from their natural prominent positions in the pace map, either could force their way forward at the start and create pressure on Handshake that destabilises the anticipated tactical scenario; a more contested gallop would scramble the race shape and potentially open the door for any runner adapting best on the day.

watchPoints.text: Handshake's uncontested lead is the hinge of the entire race — if he is allowed to dictate, he controls the tempo and the result; watch for any early challenge from Sinmara or God Of Power at the start that could fundamentally alter the shape.

God Of Power and Sinmara are natural front-runners mapped to midfield: if either pushes forward aggressively in the early stages, the anticipated moderate pace could turn contested, shortening the run-home advantage for Hazdann and lengthening Dial Me In's chance.

Hazdann returns after 85 days off — watch his market moves in the final hour before racing; Weld horses often arrive fit first time back but a drifting price could signal the team want a race into him rather than a peak performance today.

Dial Me In's finishing position will act as a barometer for how genuine the pace was — if he finishes within two lengths, the gallop was faster than the race shape suggests; if he is well beaten, Handshake's steady lead effectively dictated a result that rewarded prominent racers throughout.

races.name: Racing Here Again On September 28th Maiden

runners_data.name: Coolnagrattan
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing 4yo for W R Crawford who goes on Good ground (3 from 3 on similar), steps back to 1m4f having run over 12f and 16f before — that versatility helps — but trainer is 0 from 4 in the 14-day window and this is a tough 19-runner field for a horse rated 120 who has never won.

runners_data.name: Nothingbutadream
runners_data.note: Hold-up 4yo with a fade-in-finish flag; has finished 7th, 10th and 15th in recent starts and a 16-day turnaround on 0 wins from 3 tries suggests she needs things to fall very right — the subdued pace created by Mawhibah is unlikely to serve her well.

runners_data.name: Nugentstown Sue
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up 7yo returning from 278 days off, placed once in six similar-going runs and has finished in the top five just once in five starts at 16f — the long absence and fade flag are serious concerns against a field of younger rivals.

runners_data.name: Shemiyka
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing 4yo with headgear (visor) and a reasonable recent profile — 4th and 3rd in her last two starts over 10f and 12f — stepping back to Good from Soft; trainer M D O'Callaghan has 2 from 11 in 14 days which is adequate.

runners_data.name: Almazann
runners_data.note: Prominent-style 3yo for D K Weld who has placed in all three career starts, every one at 10f or 12f on Good — the step up to 1m4f is the only query, but the consistent placed form and capable handler make her one of the chief dangers from just off the pace.

runners_data.name: Daily Wonder
runners_data.note: Unknown profile with no public form; T G McCourt runner listed with no last-run date, making going preferences and running style entirely speculative — the 7lb claim from Sadhbh Tormey is a potential upside if she arrives well-schooled.

runners_data.name: Four Ball

runners_data.name: Nemorino
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Henry De Bromhead whose stable is in strong 14-day form (6/27); no public form data on going or style means this is a pure unknown, though De Bromhead regularly runs well-prepared first-timers at provincial tracks.

runners_data.name: Plug In Hybrid
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing 3yo for Colin Keane and Noel Meade; only one start to his name (6th at 9f on Good) but the booking of Keane — one of the country's top riders — and the step to 1m4f could suit if there is any untapped stamina.

runners_data.name: Purple Bandit
runners_data.note: Debut 3yo for Mrs John Harrington with a headgear flag (blinkers); style is unknown but Harrington's stable is active (2/28 in 14 days) and Shane Foley's booking is significant — the blinkers on debut occasionally signal a horse being produced ready.

runners_data.name: Cosmetic

runners_data.name: I Hope You Dance
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up 3yo for De Bromhead who has placed twice at 12f on contrasting surfaces; pushed into a midfield map position because the field holds too many deep-closers to accommodate all at the rear — her closing kick is likely blunted by the modest pace and the positional compromise, so her chance should be tempered accordingly.

runners_data.name: Kigalienne

runners_data.name: Mawhibah

runners_data.name: Miss Romagna

runners_data.name: Shambata

runners_data.name: Metallic

runners_data.name: Gentle Soda

runners_data.name: Michinaga
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo for Charles Weld; has run 6th and 9th in two starts, style unverified despite being marked U — 13 days since last run and no jockey confirmed; the form is quiet but the Weld connection (related stable to D K Weld) is worth a note.

races.paceDynamic: Mawhibah is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner maiden over 1m4f on Good ground at Roscommon, and with no genuine rival willing to press her for the lead she is set to control this race from the front at a pace entirely of her own choosing. Behind her, Coolnagrattan, Almazann, Plug In Hybrid, and Miss Romagna will press for prominent positions, creating a mid-to-large group tracking a single pace-setter rather than an aggressive early battle. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — I Hope You Dance is a genuine sit-and-sprint horse who will be displaced into a midfield berth, meaning her natural closing kick is likely to be compromised. With Mawhibah able to dictate an honest but not punishing tempo on a flat track, this shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader, save ground, and quicken into the straight — hold-up horses relying on a strong pace to reel in the field will find the race not run to suit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mawhibah Leads, Prompters Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Mawhibah sets a measured, uncontested pace and the prominent trackers quicken past her in the straight.
scenarios.body: Mawhibah rolls along in front without any pressure, allowing Almazann, Coolnagrattan, and Miss Romagna to settle just behind before producing their efforts entering the home straight; the honest but controlled tempo means those with the best cruising speed and a turn of foot off a sound gallop dominate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Mawhibah Bowls Along Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Mawhibah's lead is so uncontested that she steals an insurmountable advantage and holds on for a front-runner's success.
scenarios.body: The lack of any genuine challenger sees Mawhibah dictate every fraction and, with 19 rivals unable to organise a coordinated response, she maintains enough petrol in the tank to see out the 1m4f trip and hold all challengers; her JP O'Brien stable are in excellent 14-day form with 12 winners from 71.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is so slow that a bunched straight-dash develops and hold-up horses get an uncharacteristic opportunity.
scenarios.body: A crawl early compresses the field, neutralising positional advantages and turning the race into a sprint from the home turn; Cosmetic and Shambata, who prefer to come late, are the primary beneficiaries if the tempo collapses, though I Hope You Dance — mapped to midfield rather than her true rear position — carries a style-fit discount in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unknown Debutant Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If one of the several lightly-raced or debut runners (Purple Bandit, Nemorino, Daily Wonder, Kigalienne) has been produced with a well-timed preparation and proves well above maiden level.
scenarios.body: A big unknown field of 19 always carries the risk of a well-schooled newcomer arriving with a hidden rating; high-profile connections — Mrs John Harrington (Purple Bandit, Kigalienne) and Henry De Bromhead (Nemorino) — have the firepower to do this, but the race shape must still be run in a way that suits the debutant's unknown style.

watchPoints.text: Mawhibah's pace — watch whether J M Sheridan elects to bowl along at a truly honest gallop or nurses her; if she slows significantly through the middle section, closers get an unexpected invitation and the entire race shape shifts.

Almazann has finished 2nd in all three starts and is overdue a win — if D K Weld drops her in behind the pace and Colin Keane produces Plug In Hybrid wide, the two prominent-style runners may split the market and one finishes strongly enough to finally break her duck.

Purple Bandit and Kigalienne are both Harrington debutants with significant jockey bookings (Foley and McCullagh respectively); two well-prepared newcomers from the same handler in the same race is a pattern worth tracking in the market before post time.

I Hope You Dance is a genuine hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to field congestion — if Gary Carroll pushes her forward in running to compensate, watch for her to be caught in a no-man's land, neither tracking the pace efficiently nor producing a true closing run.

With 19 runners on a flat Roscommon circuit at 1m4f, early position out of the gates matters enormously — horses drawn in wider stalls (particularly any of the unknown debutants) who are slow to stride could find themselves shuffled back and facing an impossible task to recover on a track that does not generate a true strong pace today.

runners_data.name: L'Un Deux Trois

races.paceDynamic: Stellar Moment is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to press hard for the lead, should settle into a comfortable, uncontested gallop over this 1m4f trip on Good ground at Roscommon. Youcansaythatagain and Neptunes Staircase are the nearest prominent types and will track close to the pace, but neither is likely to force a true test from the front. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Lord Aus, Zoffman, Flying Fortress, Faro Island, Letiza, Ryefield Dasher, Summer Snow, Duke Of Leggagh and L'Un Deux Trois are all genuine closers but will be funnelled into midfield positions through necessity, leaving the true back-markers thinly represented. A steady, controlled pace set by a single front-runner on a flat, fair track strongly favours horses who can race prominently or at least in the first half of the field, tracking the tempo and producing a sustained run from two furlongs out rather than mounting a sweeping late challenge from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stellar Moment Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Stellar Moment bowls along unchallenged at a fair but undemanding gallop, the race becomes a procession that rewards horses close enough to her in the early stages.
scenarios.body: Stellar Moment settles the field from the front, dictating a rhythm that never truly punishes the prominent holders; when she extends approaching the straight, only those who have tracked her closely have the ground to mount a challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trio Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses — Youcansaythatagain, Neptunes Staircase and Royal Saxo — push up assertively and force a genuinely contested gallop from the front.
scenarios.body: A genuine pace duel develops in the first mile, burning off those who rely on a sprint finish and delivering a contest in the straight between the most resolute stayers who tracked the pace honestly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is only modest and horses mapped into the middle of the pack — particularly those with legitimate form — find a clear run turning in.
scenarios.body: Horses like Merlin The Wizard and Thyer, who carry strong form at the trip and going, are close enough throughout to produce a sustained finish without needing a passage through tightly packed groups.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Sweep Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely fast and runners at the front tire badly in the straight, opening ground for horses held up further back.
scenarios.body: This depends on redistributed hold-up types — Lord Aus, Faro Island, Flying Fortress — actually being allowed to settle near the back, which the field size and race shape make difficult; the scenario is possible but structurally unlikely given the pace context.

watchPoints.text: Stellar Moment holds the race shape in her hands — if Rory Mulligan (5) controls the pace confidently and hits the straight with a lead in hand, the race is unlikely to be won from behind.

Youcansaythatagain (W J Lee, OR 82) is the top-rated runner and races prominently by nature — watch whether Lee pushes up to sit second on the heels of Stellar Moment from the outset, which would confirm the dominant scenario.

Summer Snow and Duke Of Leggagh have no jockey declared — confirm declarations and rider bookings before the off, as the absence of a named pilot is a significant late-markets flag for two runners in a 19-horse field.

Lord Aus and Faro Island are the two redistributed hold-up types with the strongest underlying form — if either finds a clear run turning in, they have the ability to finish strongly, but both need traffic to part in a tightly packed midfield.

Neptunes Staircase is returning from 156 days off for Lyons and Keane — watch pre-race market moves; if the market supports this runner, fitness concerns are presumably managed, and a prominent prominent run becomes a serious threat.

races.paceDynamic: Sir Trancealot is the lone confirmed front runner in a 19-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m4f trip on Good ground at Roscommon. The pace is unlikely to be searching — a single, unchallenged pace-setter on a flat course in good ground typically sets an honest but not punishing tempo, meaning the field will be compressed and the race will be decided in the final two furlongs. The vast majority of this field are natural hold-up or midfield types, and with Canon Law, Wipeawayyourtears, Glen Echo and Augusta Rock all carrying strong form at this trip and going, the finish will be a mass sprint from a bunched pack. This race shape — moderate gallop, steady early, strong late sectionals — heavily favours horses who can travel smoothly in midfield, move into position turning for home, and sustain a finish over the distance; pure hold-up types racing far off the pace will likely find the final burst too short and compact. This field carries considerably more prominent and hold-up types than can be accommodated in their natural positions — Premier Princess, Princess Rosie, Ellens Bay and others have been redistributed to midfield on the map, but in practice they will be jostling for space and unable to travel at their preferred trip point, making their routes to the winner's enclosure harder.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Sir Trancealot sets a calm, uncontested lead and the race only quickens sharply in the final 2f, producing a bunched finish.
scenarios.body: The compressed gallop suits horses who travel economically in midfield and possess a sustained late kick over 1m4f on Good ground; the lack of genuine pressure on the pace means the field arrives at the turn in a heap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Movers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to string the field out, allowing horses travelling in the first half of the pack to pick off the leader entering the straight.
scenarios.body: A truthful gallop from Sir Trancealot on this flat track rewards those tracking in fifth to eighth and able to challenge two furlongs out without needing a dramatic late run; the Good going enables a smooth, progressive move.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Sir Trancealot is left completely unmolested and the pace is slow enough that he is never truly tested, arriving at the final furlong with a meaningful advantage.
scenarios.body: A lone front runner unchallenged in a handicap can steal this; Seamie Heffernan is experienced enough to perfectly manage fractions, and the flat Roscommon straight offers no hiding place for closers who leave too much to do.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace surprises with vigour and the field fans wide in the straight, creating a genuine opportunity for horses finishing from the rear.
scenarios.body: This scenario is discounted because the majority of apparent hold-up types are REDISTRIBUTED horses whose true style is prominent or midfield, meaning genuine closers with the sustained finish to benefit from a true end-to-end gallop are sparse in this field.

watchPoints.text: Sir Trancealot — monitor whether Seamie Heffernan attempts to control fractions from the front or is unexpectedly pressured early; if anything moves up to challenge before halfway, the race shape changes entirely and the scenario probabilities shift markedly toward Scenario B.

Canon Law — watch the market; if Rory Cleary settles this horse into a prominent position behind the leader rather than holding up as the style tag suggests, it becomes a very dangerous proposition given the exact match of win form (1/14f/GOO) to today's conditions.

Augusta Rock — Declan McDonogh is a rider who can produce big runs from redisitributed hold-up types; if the yard confidence (12/71 in 14 days) spills into the market, treat any significant move as meaningful even accounting for the style displacement.

Minella Buoy — three placed efforts over marathon trips mean stamina is not in question; if this horse travels comfortably in midfield and W J Lee asks early enough turning for home, the sustained gallop could expose rivals who fade.

Ellens Bay — a placed run over 14f on Good last time is directly relevant form that few in this field can match at the exact distance; Luke McAteer should be instructed to ignore the redistributed map position and race as naturally as possible given the trip suitability.
